15 Water from a reservoir is fed to the turbine of a hydroelectric system at a rate of 510 kg s–1. The
reservoir is 280 m above the level of the turbine.
The electrical output from the generator driven by the turbine is a current of 205 A at a potential
difference of 5800 V.
What is the efficiency of the system?
A
8.3%
B
12%
C
83%
D
85%

hints: Notice the input is falling water at $510 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$ through $280 \text{ m}$, so input power is gravitational potential energy lost per second.
Connect mass per second to power with $P_{in} = mgh/t = (m/t)gh$ using $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Connect the $205 \text{ A}$ and $5800 \text{ V}$ output to electrical power with $P_{out} = IV$, then use $efficiency = P_{out}/P_{in}$.
walkthrough: Identify input power as rate of loss of gravitational potential energy: $P_{in} = (m/t)gh$, with $m/t = 510 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$ and $h = 280 \text{ m}$.
Substitute with units: $P_{in} = 510 \times 9.81 \times 280$ in $\text{W}$, which gives $P_{in} \approx 1.40 \times 10^6 \text{ W}$.
Identify useful output power as electrical power: $P_{out} = IV$, with $I = 205 \text{ A}$ and $V = 5800 \text{ V}$.
Substitute: $P_{out} = 205 \times 5800 = 1.189 \times 10^6 \text{ W}$, with units of $\text{W}$ on both powers so the ratio is valid.
Calculate efficiency $= P_{out}/P_{in} = 1.189 \times 10^6 / 1.401 \times 10^6 \approx 0.849$, or $84.9\%$ which rounds to $85\%$. This is option D.

A.explanation: This is about 10 times too small and results from a power-of-ten error when combining $510 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$, $280 \text{ m}$ and $205 \text{ A}$ at $5800 \text{ V}$.

B.explanation: This is the reciprocal ratio, input power divided by output power expressed incorrectly, giving about $1/0.85$ scaled as a percentage.

C.explanation: This is close but low because it uses $g = 10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ for input power instead of $9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, giving about $1.19/1.43$.

D.explanation: Output power $IV$ divided by input power $(mass/time)gh$ is about $1.19 \times 10^6 / 1.40 \times 10^6 = 0.85$, or $85\%$.
